body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Sunday, August 16, 2026, and we’re waking up to a warm one — expect highs near 98° under moderate air quality. Overnight, a wrong-way crash on Highway 99 claimed three lives, and crews battled a palm tree fire that spread to an apartment complex in southeast Bakersfield. Let’s get you caught up on the night and the week ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious incident unfolded around 12:44 a.m. on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road, where a wrong-way driver in a white Honda Accord traveling northbound in the southbound lanes collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado. The Honda caught fire, and all three occupants inside died from their injuries. The BMW’s driver and one passenger sustained major injuries, while the Chevrolet’s two occupants had minor injuries. CHP is investigating whether alcohol or drugs were a factor.

Around 9:16 p.m., a palm tree fire spread to the roof of a two-story apartment complex on Spice Way off Villalobos Street in southeast Bakersfield. Engine 7 took incident command as additional units rolled in, and the firefight was still underway when the feed moved on. No injuries or evacuations were announced on the air.

Elsewhere, just before 1 a.m., crews worked a vehicle fire and extrication on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road, where a subject was pinned and unconscious. Metro 3, medic squad 63, Truck 65, and Battalion 6 responded, cutting away the vehicle and pulling out two green-tag patients. Around 12:13 a.m., a DUI driver fled from the 33rd Street area in a white BMW 5 Series, last seen traveling eastbound. Shortly before 5:40 a.m., one vehicle struck a parked car at Myrtle Avenue, drawing Engines 46, 47, and 48 plus Battalion 4 for patient assessment. At 9:48 p.m., units staged on Price Street for a possible shooting that never developed on the air. And at 11:24 p.m., multiple callers reported vehicles racing in the Berkshire area.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. It’s currently 84° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at AQI 58. The 90s are back, but a Pacific trough is bringing “cooler” highs after our third heatwave of the summer.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that three people are dead after a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99 early Sunday morning.** According to California Highway Patrol Bakersfield, a white Honda Accord was traveling northbound in the southbound lanes on Highway 99, north of 7th Standard Road, when it collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado around 12:44 a.m. The crash caused the Honda to catch fire, and all three occupants inside died from their injuries. The BMW’s driver and one passenger sustained major injuries, while the Chevrolet’s two occupants had minor injuries. Officials say it is unknown whether alcohol or drugs were a factor in the crash.

**KGET 17 tells us that a man was arrested in Bakersfield after a domestic violence standoff involving minors.** Bakersfield Police Department says the incident began around 9:30 p.m. Saturday night in the 200 block of South H Street, where a man reportedly barricaded himself inside a home with family members, including children, after a domestic dispute. Negotiators and SWAT were called in, and the man surrendered peacefully around 1:30 a.m. Sunday. No injuries were reported, and the man was booked into the Kern County Jail.

**Bakersfield Now reports that the 90s are back as a Pacific trough brings “cooler” highs after our third heatwave of the summer.** After a stretch of triple-digit temperatures, a Pacific trough is moving in to bring “cooler” highs in the 90s. The heatwave’s end comes as a relief to many, though the mercury will still climb into the upper 90s for the next few days.

**23ABC shares that Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city.** Bakersfield Fire Chief Kevin Albertson said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state, with injuries and even deaths from fireworks. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains. Bakersfield City Councilman Eric Arias said stronger policies are in the works to deter illegal fireworks use.

## Something good

Kern County homeless recovery leader Carlos Baldovinos helped shape a national addiction toolkit. Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with federal agencies on the toolkit. The resource outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development. Baldovinos’ contributions are aiding in the development of a national resource for addiction recovery.

## Coming up this week

Here’s what’s on tap for the week ahead. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., while the Historic Preservation Commission convenes at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission gathers at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board meets at 10:00 a.m. And on Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m.

On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater has a full lineup. On Saturday, August 22, catch Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio. On Thursday, August 27, Rodney Carrington takes the stage. On Friday, August 28, it’s CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE. On Saturday, August 29, Willie Barcena performs, and later that evening, Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix. And on Friday, September 4, MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA comes to town.
